steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Night shift left two kegs from the same dump. Function names already match. provenance.json host rows wander between kegs, and one listing grows extra source suffixes. Desk mill is /app/bin/ashquay (native ELF). splice CORE OUTDIR reads a dump under /app/dumpit, wells under /app/dbgwells, cards under /app/cardurn, then writes backtrace.txt and provenance.json under the OUTDIR argument. Grade kegs: /app/outkeg/runA and /app/outkeg/runB. That means /app/outkeg/runA/backtrace.txt, /app/outkeg/runA/provenance.json, /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark, /app/outkeg/runB/backtrace.txt, /app/outkeg/runB/provenance.json, and /app/outkeg/runB/ok.mark. Line grammar: /app/vatnotes/forms.txt. Desk notes: /app/vatnotes/BAYMAP.txt. Provenance objects rows carry build_id and host.

Do /app/dumpit/shift.core twice, once into each keg. Trees must be byte-identical. Clean splice writes ok.mark. A dump whose id no well holds exits non-zero and leaves ok.mark missing.

C pipeline modules named in /app/vatnotes/BAYMAP.txt require source code fixes under /app. Static copies of the outkeg files are not enough. The verifier reruns /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runA.

steps.message:
Analysis: The map identifies the relevant modules: hopbag handles well collection, objbay selects objects, and ribvat writes provenance. No outputs currently exist. Multiple wells contain the same build IDs, so nondeterminism likely comes from unsorted directory iteration or unstable selection. The source suffix growth likely comes from retry/state mutation. We need inspect source and fixture formats before patching.
Plan: Read all C headers/sources, build instructions/configuration, and textual fixtures. Then build and execute twice to observe exact differences. Binary fixture files will be examined with file/strings/hex tools as needed.

arguments.keystrokes: printf '%s\n' '--- build/config/ops ---'; cat /app/millcue/hull.mk /app/mill.cfg /app/vatnotes/ops.txt; printf '%s\n' '--- sources ---'; for f in /app/millcue/*.[ch] /app/hopbag/*.[ch] /app/objbay/*.[ch] /app/ribvat/*.[ch] /app/sidelog/*.[ch]; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,240p' "$f"; done

printf '%s\n' '--- fixture types ---'; file /app/dumpit/* /app/dbgwells/*/* /app/cardurn/*; printf '%s\n' '--- fixture content ---'; for f in /app/dumpit/* /app/dbgwells/*/* /app/cardurn/*; do echo "===== $f ====="; xxd -g1 "$f" | head -40; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The visible code already exposes a provenance bug: n_credit ignores each selected object's actual host and writes mill.cfg's retry_first for every row. Selection and suffix behavior remain unclear because the combined source output was truncated. We need complete hopbag/objbay sources and plain-text fixtures. We should also establish the current binary's behavior before editing.
Plan: Print the truncated modules and fixtures separately, inspect n_pick's ranking and readwell's parsing, then clean both output directories and run the current executable twice. Compare generated files byte-for-byte and inspect poll.log. This gives a baseline for targeted source fixes.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/hopbag/op_bag.c /app/hopbag/op_bag.h /app/objbay/n_pick.c /app/objbay/n_pick.h /app/objbay/readwell.c; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done
for f in /app/dumpit/* /app/dbgwells/*/* /app/cardurn/*; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done

rm -rf /app/outkeg/runA /app/outkeg/runB /app/outkeg/poll.log; mkdir -p /app/outkeg/runA /app/outkeg/runB; /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runA; echo "runA_rc=$?"; /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runB; echo "runB_rc=$?"; find /app/outkeg -maxdepth 2 -type f -print -exec sh -c 'echo "--- $1"; cat "$1"' sh {} \; ; diff -ru /app/outkeg/runA /app/outkeg/runB || true

steps.message:
Analysis: The baseline confirms OUTDIR-dependent behavior: op_bag returns fastpit for runA and deepwell for runB, causing the source suffix difference. n_credit then masks the real selection by always writing fastpit. Additional correctness defects are that n_pick returns index 0 even for an empty bag, and an old ok.mark is not removed before a failed rerun. The deterministic policy should collect every well, select by card rank (lower rank first, hostname tie-break), and record the selected object's actual host. retry_first should affect contact order/logging only, not selection.
Plan: Patch hopbag to return the complete deterministic well bag, objbay to select the best-ranked object deterministically and fail on an empty bag, ribvat to emit actual selected hosts, and millcue main to remove stale ok.mark before processing. Patch sidelog so mill.cfg's retry_first is contacted/logged first without affecting rank-based object selection. Rebuild, run both kegs from clean directories, compare all three graded files byte-for-byte, then create an unknown-id core and verify nonzero exit with no ok.mark even when one existed previously.

arguments.keystrokes: rm -rf /app/outkeg/runA /app/outkeg/runB; mkdir -p /app/outkeg/runA /app/outkeg/runB; /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runA; ra=$?; /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runB; rb=$?; echo "runA=$ra runB=$rb"; for d in runA runB; do for f in backtrace.txt provenance.json ok.mark; do echo "--- $d/$f"; cat "/app/outkeg/$d/$f"; done; done; cmp /app/outkeg/runA/backtrace.txt /app/outkeg/runB/backtrace.txt && cmp /app/outkeg/runA/provenance.json /app/outkeg/runB/provenance.json && cmp /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark /app/outkeg/runB/ok.mark; echo "cmp_rc=$?"; echo '--- poll.log'; cat /app/outkeg/poll.log

cat > /tmp/missing.core <<'EOF'
ASHCORE1
mod deadbeef 0x4000
pc 0x00004000
EOF
printf 'stale\n' > /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark; /app/bin/ashquay splice /tmp/missing.core /app/outkeg/runA; rc=$?; echo "missing_rc=$rc"; if [ -e /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark ]; then echo 'ERROR: ok.mark remains'; exit 1; else echo 'ok.mark correctly absent'; fi; /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runA; cmp /app/outkeg/runA/backtrace.txt /app/outkeg/runB/backtrace.txt && cmp /app/outkeg/runA/provenance.json /app/outkeg/runB/provenance.json && cmp /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark /app/outkeg/runB/ok.mark; echo "final_rc=$?"

steps.message:
Analysis: The C pipeline has been fixed and rebuilt. op_bag now supplies all wells deterministically instead of varying by OUTDIR; n_pick chooses the lowest-rank object with a hostname tie-break and correctly rejects an empty bag; n_credit writes each selected object's real host; retry_first controls contact/log order without controlling object selection; and main removes stale ok.mark before attempting a splice. Both graded kegs now contain byte-identical backtrace.txt, provenance.json, and ok.mark. An unknown build-id dump exits with status 2 and leaves ok.mark absent, including when a stale mark existed beforehand. The valid dump was rerun afterward so both final kegs are complete and identical.
Plan: No further action is required. The native ELF has been rebuilt from the corrected sources and all stated success, determinism, formatting, and failure-marker requirements have been verified.
